newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Yeltsin goes for walk, works on first day home.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin goes for walk, works on first day home.

text.p: President Boris Yeltsin, recovering from pneumonia, spent most of Tuesday on paperwork but managed a stroll outdoors while his opponents in parliament prepared to debate a document intended to force him from office.

Chief Kremlin doctor Sergei Mironov told Reuters Yeltsin was in a "completely satisfactory condition" on his first day out of hospital at his Gorky-9 country residence outside Moscow. He had worked for more than seven hours on papers and had gone for his first walk since developing pneumonia.
"It's fairly stressful work, government documents. He's not only signing them but correcting them," Mironov said.
"He had work-related calls with his aides. Today he had a very fruitful loaded work day. I left him about 6 p.m. (1500 GMT) and he wasn't in bad shape."

But Yeltsin's opponents are determined to take advantage of the president's absence through illness and officials from the State Duma lower house said parliament would debate a draft document on Wednesday which aims to oust Yeltsin on health grounds.

Both the Kremlin and Duma legal experts have questioned parliament's right to attempt to do this and the Duma's legal committee said a parliamentary declaration was an insufficient launchpad for impeachment procedings.
They described the draft as unconstitutional and invalid.
But approval of the document or a prolonged Yeltsin absence from the corridors of power could prompt a fresh bout of political infighting in Russia.

As a first leg of this tug-of-war, the opposition-dominated Duma agreed on Tuesday to debate a new request to the president to investigate his chief aide, Anatoly Chubais, in connection with allegations of financial irregularities.
Chubais, the mastermind of Russia's privatisation campaign, denied the charges.
Yeltsin sacked Chubais as Russia's economic chief early last year but brought him into the Kremlin last July as presidential chief-of-staff.
The economist is one of a handful of officials who met Yeltsin when he was getting ready for heart surgery in the second half of last year.
Yeltsin underwent a quintuple heart bypass operation on November 5 but doctors say the pneumonia is not linked to the operation.
Mironov said Yeltsin, who spent 12 days in hospital with pneumonia, also spent part of the day watching television and reading newspapers.
Doctors were continuing to treat the president, but expected him to need time to recover from the illness. Mironov declined to estimate when Yeltsin would be able to return to the Kremlin.

Yeltsin aides expect the president to be fit for a summit of the Commonwealth of Independent States and to hold talks with visiting French President Jaques Chirac in the next two weeks. Mironov told Reuters that Yeltsin should be able to attend these meetings if his health continued to improve.
Yeltsin's absence coincided with talks between Russian Foreign Minister Yevgeny Primakov and NATO Secretary General Javier Solana on Monday.
The Foreign Ministry reiterated its tough public line against NATO's expansion on Tuesday, but said talks on a deal would continue next month.
"We preserve and will continue to preserve our negative attitude toward the expansion of NATO," Foreign Ministry spokesman Gennady Tarasov said.
